text: Where does the buyer type their card number: on the shop's site, or on the bank's?
prefix: Where does the buyer type their card number: on the shop's site, or on the bank's?

text: If shops collected card numbers, every shop would need PCI DSS, and one shop's breach would leak cards.
prefix: If shops collected card numbers, every shop would need PCI DSS, and one shop's breach would leak cards.

text: So the merchant sends the buyer to the bank's own payment page, through the one-time link it got when it created the payment.
prefix: So the merchant sends the buyer to the bank's own payment page, through the one-time link it got when it created the payment.

text: The link's token is the only credential: the database keeps only its hash, and after the configured time the link works no more.
prefix: The link's token is the only credential: the database keeps only its hash, and after the configured time the link works no more.

text: Reading the page changes nothing: it shows the website's name and logo, the amount, the order, and the cards the website accepts.
prefix: Reading the page changes nothing: it shows the website's name and logo, the amount, the order, and the cards the website accepts.

text: The buyer types the card, and the BIN module names its scheme and bank first, so a card the website doesn't accept never gets a code.
prefix: The buyer types the card, and the BIN module names its scheme and bank first, so a card the website doesn't accept never gets a code.

text: The card module checks the Luhn digit, stores the number encrypted, and asks the card's scheme, through its adapter, to send a one-time code; Humo reads the card first, and sends it only to an active card's mobile banking phone.
prefix: The card module checks the Luhn digit, stores the number encrypted, and asks the card's scheme, through its adapter, to send a one-time code; Humo reads the card first, and sends it only to an active card's mobile banking phone.

text: Each code gets its own binding, so two payments with the same card never overwrite each other's code.
prefix: Each code gets its own binding, so two payments with the same card never overwrite each other's code.

text: The page now shows the bank, the scheme and the card's last four digits, kept in the payment's card columns, and waits for the code.
prefix: The page now shows the bank, the scheme and the card's last four digits, kept in the payment's card columns, and waits for the code.

text: The right code confirms the card through the same scheme, a card the scheme reports as blocked or expired is never bound, and the payment is ready to debit.
prefix: The right code confirms the card through the same scheme, a card the scheme reports as blocked or expired is never bound, and the payment is ready to debit.

text: Every attempt is counted, and committed before the scheme is asked, so a failed attempt still counts.
prefix: Every attempt is counted, and committed before the scheme is asked, so a failed attempt still counts.

text: Three cards, and three codes for each card, are allowed, and both numbers are configuration.
prefix: Three cards, and three codes for each card, are allowed, and both numbers are configuration.

text: When the last attempt fails, the page closes for good.
prefix: When the last attempt fails, the page closes for good.

text: One step runs at a time: a second click while the scheme is still answering is refused by a lock in Redis, which only its holder releases, and which outlives the slowest scheme call.
prefix: One step runs at a time: a second click while the scheme is still answering is refused by a lock in Redis, which only its holder releases, and which outlives the slowest scheme call.
